decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Selling Mineral Rights: Timeline In 2026
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 28922213d449f95874fbd6a8fa7e55963eb5fbb63f2321f2bab02b2f879402ae; all 7 declared sources passed live access review.

MRX claims remain bounded to the published Texas-timeline and nationwide-process companions and current methodology; IRS claims remain bounded to general disposition, basis-record, and Form 1099-S instruction distinctions; the FBI claim remains bounded to independent verification of unexpected account or payment-instruction changes.

The article uses no fabricated owners, buyers, deeds, payments, prices, acreage, ownership decimals, deadlines, settlement records, recording numbers, testimonials, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, accounting, valuation, cybersecurity, escrow, investment, or transaction conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, How Long Does It Take to Sell Mineral Rights in Texas? (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX Texas timeline article explains that no single Texas sale duration applies and identifies ownership records, buyer diligence, contract conditions, curative work, signing, payment, deed delivery, and recording as timing dependencies.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: Wave 31 uses that page only as a state-specific companion and keeps its own job nationwide and centered on dependency lanes, completion evidence, critical-path changes, and reforecasting; it does not restate Texas conveyance, recording, or production-data law.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Selling Mineral Rights: Selling Process For Mineral Owners (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX nationwide seller-control article gives each transaction stage a required input, owner decision, written output, and stop condition and distinguishes signing, funding, delivery, acceptance, and recording.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: Wave 31 uses that page as the process-architecture companion while owning the dated planning calendar, controller lanes, parallel-work distinctions, completion evidence, and reset rules; it does not repeat the full stage-control instructions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology identifies production history, decline context, operator evidence, royalty terms, commodity assumptions, discount rate, title and acreage, and any offer terms as dated inputs to a directional range with assumptions stated.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the methodology only to explain why timeline inputs need source and retrieval dates and why corrected or newer evidence can trigger a reforecast; it does not calculate value, prove title or reserves, guarantee an outcome, or recommend a transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 544, Sales and Other Dispositions of Assets (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Publication 544 explains that tax treatment and reporting for a sale or other disposition depend on the property, its use, the holding period, the parties, and other transaction facts.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the publication only to require a transaction-specific tax handoff and final record archive; it does not classify the owner’s asset, compute gain or loss, select a tax form, or state an owner-specific tax result.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 551, Basis of Assets (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Publication 551 describes basis as an amount used for tax computations including depletion and gain or loss and directs taxpayers to keep accurate records of items affecting basis.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the publication only to require preservation of basis-relevant records and a qualified tax handoff; it does not calculate basis, depletion, gain, loss, liability, or a retention period for a specific owner.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Instructions for Form 1099-S (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current Instructions for Form 1099-S provide transaction-specific rules for reporting sales or exchanges of real estate and address ownership interests, exceptions, reporting persons, and multiple transferors.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the instructions only to support a dated tax-professional and information-reporting handoff; it does not conclude whether a mineral owner will receive Form 1099-S or how a sale must be reported.

sources_inspected.label: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center, Business Email Compromise (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center explains that business email compromise can target businesses and individuals transferring funds and recommends a secondary channel or two-factor authentication to verify requests that change account information.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that guidance for a bounded payment-instruction verification step; it does not provide cybersecurity, banking, escrow, fraud-investigation, or loss-recovery advice or guarantee that a payment channel is safe.
